note: Attacker-controlled value of the 'lxc.rootfs.options' config key (an 'idmap=' mount option whose path value is >= PATH_MAX bytes) is read from the input config file and dispatched to the config setter.
The user-controlled mount-options string is duplicated into a heap buffer that is passed to the parser.
The unvalidated mount-options string reaches the vulnerable LXC mount-option parser.
The parser locates the 'idmap=' LXC specific mount option inside the attacker-controlled string.

Root cause: the size argument passed to strlcpy() is 'idmap_path - p2 + 1', i.e. the full attacker-controlled idmap value length plus one, and is never bounded by sizeof(opts->userns_path) (PATH_MAX). strlcpy() therefore writes idmap_path - p2 + 1 bytes into the 4096-byte userns_path destination when the idmap path is >= PATH_MAX bytes long; the length check on the strlcpy() return value happens only after the overflowing copy.
The post-copy bound check is too late: it uses the strlcpy() return value (full source length) after the destination buffer has already been overrun.
Sink: with len == idmap_path - p2 (the full attacker-controlled idmap path length, e.g. 5000), memcpy() writes len bytes past the 4096-byte opts->userns_path heap buffer, causing the buffer overrun.
